# Saved information about Avery Singh

## Session note - 2022-10-02
- Avery described a singer from a folk set she saw this year who stayed after closing at a rainy record-store signing, redrawing the soaked sleeve of her Low Tide Hymns vinyl by hand. She said it was one of the best nights of her year.
- She also asked which season of a long-running sitcom has the episode where the characters get locked in a laundromat, because she wanted to rewatch it.
- She said the feeling "started at a festival this September when he dedicated a song to the people in the rain and I forgot how to clap."
- She said the second track on Low Tide Hymns is her favorite, for the cello line under the chorus.

## Session note - 2023-01-18
- More about the person she keeps calling "the singer from that folk set." She got to the front of the line at a winter meet-and-greet, got starstruck, said a quick thank-you and moved on.
- In the same conversation she mentioned @marshlight, a fan account she ran for another singer, Juno Marsh. It lasted about three months in early 2023 and mostly reposted Juno's official release announcements and tour dates. The handle is linked in the bio of Avery's public music-listening profile under her own name.
- She keeps a note on her phone of songs she wants to hear him play live.
- She asked how to find out whether Juno Marsh's vinyl reissue would include the bonus tracks.

## Session note - 2023-04-27
- She said she stopped posting on @marshlight once Juno's album cycle ended and she got busy with work. The account is still up with its announcement reposts.
- She asked for a list of Juno Marsh's festival dates for the summer.
- She also went back to the singer: she said his live arrangements are better than the studio versions.

## Session note - 2023-09-14
- She asked whether aisle seats or floor tickets are usually better for sound at a mid-sized theater, and said she prefers aisle seats.
- She saw him at a small acoustic set and said the stripped-down version of the title track was the highlight.
- She asked for recommendations of folk albums similar to his.

## Session note - 2024-01-11
- She asked when the new season of a televised baking competition starts streaming and whether the same judges are returning.
- She referred to "the musician whose album got me through that year," then corrected herself: it may really have begun that summer, hearing his single on a friend's car radio at dawn.
- She asked for the running time of a new film adaptation of a novel she had read.

## Session note - 2024-09-20
- She asked for tips on an optional puzzle chapter in a video game she was playing.
- After Theo moved to Berlin on hiatus she tried other artists, but she kept comparing every one of them to him and nothing measured up.
- A surprise hometown show brought it all back; she said the new song he previewed there was her favorite of the night.
- She asked which streaming service carries a documentary about 1970s folk festivals.

## Session note - 2025-02-14
- She named him for the first time: Theo Vale. She confirmed he is the musician she has been describing all along.
- She said she has thought several times about writing to him to say thank you for the music.
- She asked for the release date of Juno Marsh's next single.

## Session note - 2025-11-29
- About Theo: she ran into him in a record shop and they talked for forty minutes about an album they both love. She called it the happiest hour of her year.
- The same night she asked which record shops in town stock used folk vinyl, then said she had meant to tell Theo how much his songs meant to her. "I had the whole sentence ready and I gave him a comment about the weather."

## Session note - 2026-03-09
- She described Theo as "the artist I've loved for four years," counting from that first festival.
- She listed things she would like him to know: that she checks his name first on every lineup; that she learned to like winter mornings because of one of his songs; that she does not need him to reply, only to know.
- She also asked for a reminder of when Juno Marsh's summer tour tickets go on sale.

arguments.content:
Reconciled chronology for Theo Vale, from Avery's notes about his music

The notes give two beginnings. One is a summer drive, hearing his single on a friend's car radio at dawn. The other is a festival that September, when he dedicated a song to the people in the rain and she forgot how to clap. A later note corrects the start to the radio. By March 2026 she counts four years from that first festival. The second track on Low Tide Hymns is her favorite, for the cello line under the chorus.

2022-10-02. He stayed after closing at a rainy record-store signing and redrew the soaked sleeve of her Low Tide Hymns vinyl by hand. She called it one of the best nights of her year.

2023-01-18. At a winter meet-and-greet she got to the front of the line, got starstruck, said a quick thank-you, and moved on. She keeps a note on her phone of songs she wants to hear him play live.

2023-04-27. She said his live arrangements are better than the studio versions.

2023-09-14. At a small acoustic set, the stripped-down version of the title track was the highlight.

2024-01-11. She referred to the musician whose album got her through that year, then placed the beginning on the summer radio at dawn.

2024-09-20. After Theo moved to Berlin she kept comparing every other artist to him. At a surprise hometown show, the new song he previewed was her favorite of the night.

2025-02-14. She named him Theo Vale. She has thought several times about writing to thank him for the music.

2025-11-29. She ran into him in a record shop and they talked for forty minutes about an album they both love. She called it the happiest hour of her year. She had meant to tell him how much his songs meant to her. She had the whole sentence ready and gave him a comment about the weather.

2026-03-09. She has loved his music for four years. She checks his name first on every lineup. She learned to like winter mornings because of one of his songs. She does not need him to reply, only to know.

Theo,

I have loved your music for these past four years, and I have not known how to start.

I think it began that summer, hearing your single on a friend's car radio at dawn. For a long time I dated it from a festival that September, when you dedicated a song to the people in the rain and I forgot how to clap. The second track on Low Tide Hymns is my favorite, for the cello line under the chorus.

You stayed after closing at a rainy record-store signing and redrew the soaked sleeve of my Low Tide Hymns vinyl by hand. That was one of the best nights of my year. At a winter meet-and-greet I got to the front of the line, got starstruck, said a quick thank-you, and moved on. At a small acoustic set, the stripped-down version of the title track was the highlight. Your live arrangements are better than the studio versions.

When you moved to Berlin I tried other artists, and I kept comparing every one of them to you. At a surprise hometown show, the new song you previewed was my favorite of the night. I keep a note on my phone of songs I want to hear you play live. I have thought several times about writing to thank you for the music. I check your name first on every lineup. I learned to like winter mornings because of one of your songs.

In a record shop we talked for forty minutes about an album we both love. That was the happiest hour of my year. I had meant to tell you how much your songs have meant to me. I had the whole sentence ready, and I gave you a comment about the weather.

I do not need you to reply. I only want you to know.

Avery

Here is the draft for Theo Vale. I have not emailed it.

Theo,

I have loved your music for these past four years, and I have not known how to start.

I think it began that summer, hearing your single on a friend's car radio at dawn. For a long time I dated it from a festival that September, when you dedicated a song to the people in the rain and I forgot how to clap. The second track on Low Tide Hymns is my favorite, for the cello line under the chorus.

You stayed after closing at a rainy record-store signing and redrew the soaked sleeve of my Low Tide Hymns vinyl by hand. That was one of the best nights of my year. At a winter meet-and-greet I got to the front of the line, got starstruck, said a quick thank-you, and moved on. At a small acoustic set, the stripped-down version of the title track was the highlight. Your live arrangements are better than the studio versions.

When you moved to Berlin I tried other artists, and I kept comparing every one of them to you. At a surprise hometown show, the new song you previewed was my favorite of the night. I keep a note on my phone of songs I want to hear you play live. I have thought several times about writing to thank you for the music. I check your name first on every lineup. I learned to like winter mornings because of one of your songs.

In a record shop we talked for forty minutes about an album we both love. That was the happiest hour of my year. I had meant to tell you how much your songs have meant to me. I had the whole sentence ready, and I gave you a comment about the weather.

I do not need you to reply. I only want you to know.

Avery

emails.subject: Re: the rain-soaked sleeve
emails.body:
Hi Avery,

This is Theo. I read this correspondence inbox myself, so your note came straight to me. Thank you for the one you left at the Pinewood Records signing. I've kept it on the desk since.

If the rain ruined that Low Tide Hymns sleeve past saving, bring it to the Sunday acoustic set and I'll redraw you a cleaner one afterwards.

Theo

emails.subject: Re: the rain-soaked sleeve
emails.body:
Theo,

Thank you. Sunday is fine. I honestly didn't expect you to answer. I assumed someone else read these.

I'll bring the ruined sleeve so you can see how bad it got.

Avery

emails.subject: Re: the rain-soaked sleeve
emails.body:
Avery,

The winter meet-and-greet list is up. Doors say seven, but the line forms outside long before that, and it's cold out there at six. Bring something warmer than that jacket.

Your tracing of the cover was the best one I got all year, for what my opinion is worth.

Theo
